absent.note: Murata's specification states no DC-bias capacitance change for this C0G part, in a table or otherwise. Murata's product data flags separately downloadable characteristic data files (isECD, isSparameter and isNetList true; isBasicCharacteristicGraph and isFrequencyCharacteristicGraph false); those files are not the specification and are not cited here, so no figure is recorded.

Murata's specification has no absolute-maximum table. Its Rating cautions bound the voltage between the terminations, surges and pulses included, by the rated voltage, which the record carries as ratings.recommended.voltage_rating; the voltage-proof test level is a production test, not a rating, and the storage conditions are for unmounted parts' solderability, not a storage-temperature limit.

description: 5.6 nF +/-5% 50 V C0G MLCC, EIA 0402 (1005M), 0 +/-30 ppm/K, Murata GRM series, 180 mm paper reel
notes:
Benchmark (b) uses this part as compensation capacitor /c_c1 (C6).

C0G is a class-I dielectric, so the record carries temperature_coefficient (0 +/-30 ppm/K over 25 to 125 degC) rather than a class-II temperature_characteristic, plus Table A's capacitance-change limits at -55, -30 and -10 degC under a non-vocabulary key. Murata publishes no absolute-maximum table: the rated voltage, which Murata says must also bound surges and pulses, is ratings.recommended.voltage_rating.

pins.description: End termination 1. No polarity is marked; the two terminations are interchangeable.

provenance.note: Record default. The cited source is Murata's per-part specification (reference sheet) for this part-number family; it covers every packaging code, and the packaging letter in /mpn selects one reel. Every value here is read from it unless a deeper entry says otherwise. Pin naming and roles are the record's convention (see /pins).

/lifecycle.locator: productionStatus field of the part's product data, shown on the pim.murata.com product details page
/lifecycle.note: Murata lists the production status as In Production (the productionStatus value available); active is the lifecycle vocabulary's word for it, a mapping rather than Murata's own word. The source is the JSON the product details page renders, fetched by POST to the cited URL with body {"searchCondClass":2,"partNum":"GRM1555C1H562JE01#","page":1,"pageSize":20,"productCategoryId":"ceramicCapacitorSMD","languageRegion":"en-us","series":"","sortKey":"","valSearchCondList":[],"rangeValSearchCondList":[],"dateRangeSearchCondList":[]}; the details page itself is a script shell whose bytes carry no product data.

/mpn.locator: page 2, MURATA Part No. System; page 2, Package table (packaging code D)
/mpn.note: The specification is titled for the family GRM1555C1H562JE01_, the trailing character standing for the packaging code. The record is the orderable member with code D (180 mm reel, paper tape W8P2, 10000 pcs), a code the Package table lists; Murata's product data for GRM1555C1H562JE01# (source murata-pim-grm1555c1h562je01-2026-10-24) lists GRM1555C1H562JE01D among its orderable part numbers.

/package.note: Murata prints the size code as 1005M(0402); the record's package name is the EIA inch code, 0402, and the two terminations are the pin count.

/parameters/capacitance.locator: page 2, Rated Value table, Capacitance and Capacitance Tolerance columns; page 3, Specifications and Test Methods item 6 (Capacitance)
/parameters/capacitance.note: The nominal 5600 pF is the Capacitance column (and the part number's 562 code). min and max are that nominal at the +/-5 % tolerance, arithmetic on stated values, so datasheet-derived. The conditions are the measurement conditions of the Capacitance test item: room temperature, 1.0 +/-0.1 kHz (written as its range, 0.9 to 1.1 kHz), 1.0 +/-0.2 Vrms.

/parameters/capacitance_change_vs_temper.locator: page 6, Table A (Capacitance Change between at Reference Temp. and at each Temp.), row 5C; page 3, Specifications and Test Methods item 8 (Temperature Characteristics of Capacitance)
/parameters/capacitance_change_vs_temper.note: Table A's Max. and Min. columns for characteristic 5C at -55, -30 and -10 degC, relative to the 25 degC reference, with no DC bias and under 1.0 Vrms (item 8), written as fractions: 0.58 % is 0.0058. Not a checker-reliable key; recorded so the part's behaviour below 25 degC is not left implicit.

/parameters/capacitance_tolerance.locator: page 2, Rated Value table, Capacitance Tolerance column
/parameters/capacitance_tolerance.note: +/-5% written as a fraction of nominal.

/parameters/temperature_coefficient.locator: page 2, Rated Value table, Temp. coeff. or Cap. Change, Temp. Range and Ref.Temp. columns; page 3, Specifications and Test Methods item 8 (Temperature Characteristics of Capacitance)
/parameters/temperature_coefficient.note: Murata states 0 +/-30 ppm/degC over 25 to 125 degC about a 25 degC reference, measured with no DC bias and under 1.0 Vrms; a degC difference is a K, so the unit is ppm/K. The 0 is the class's nominal, not a typical, so no typ is recorded. Below the reference temperature Murata gives capacitance-change limits instead (Table A), recorded under capacitance_change_vs_temperature.

/pins.note: Murata publishes no pin table for a chip capacitor. Its Type & Dimension drawing shows two identical end terminations with no polarity mark, so the record names them 1 and 2 and gives both role passive, as the authoring convention does for every two-terminal passive. The numbering is the record's, not Murata's.

/ratings/recommended/ambient_temperature.locator: page 2, Rated Value table, Operating Temp. Range column; page 12, Rating section 4 (Type of Applied Voltage and Self-heating Temperature)
/ratings/recommended/ambient_temperature.note: Murata's operating temperature range. Its Rating cautions hold the capacitor's own surface temperature, self-heating included, inside this range, so as a bound on ambient it is optimistic by whatever self-heating the circuit causes.

/ratings/recommended/voltage_rating.locator: page 2, Rated Value table, Rated Voltage column; page 3, Specifications and Test Methods item 1 (Rated Voltage); page 11, Rating section 3 (Applied Voltage)
/ratings/recommended/voltage_rating.note: DC 50 V. Murata defines the rated voltage as the most that may be applied continuously; with AC superimposed the larger of the peak-to-peak and zero-to-peak voltages must stay within it, and the Rating cautions extend the bound to surges, static and pulses. Recorded as max: it is the vendor's limit for the design.
